37 · Frank Ward · Mar 87
The 1988 Championship 5 3/4 was won by Frank Ward - whose main problem appeared to be in following the correct route. Soon after leaving the common, Frank and runner-up Marcello went off course.
Apart from a fine win by Gary Staines at Wimbledon and an excellent series of races by Frank Ward who finished in 4th place overall, Belgrave lacked support from the better athletes.
The highlight of this low key part one of the Surrey Track and Field Championships was Frank Ward's bronze medal in the 10,000 metres with Roger Alsop in 6th place passing the '5000' mark in a pb.
He took the A race comfortably in the first two BAL 5000m races, backed up well by Frank Ward (2), also shown left, in match 1 and Ollie Foote in match 2.

Frank Ward did well to finish 3rd in the 5000m and as temperatures soared to the highest of the summer so far, Ollie Foote showed great judgement to gradually pick off all the opposition and sprint home a clear winner in the 10,000m, running a 62 second last lap.

Frank Ward, Ephriam Sibisi, Brian Pritchard, Colin Pearson, Marcello Bizio, Sue and Harry Porter, Bill Lucas, Leo Coy, Hazel Mead, Arthur Whitehead, Lionel Mann and family, Mark Padfield, Daye Donovan, Bert Stroud, Vic (Dick) Law, Gordon Doubleday, Eric Hall, Dermot Williamson, John Mather, John Bic…

Apart from Staines' performance there were good Belgrave supporting roles from Steve Harris, making his debut in Belgrave colours in 5th place but unable to score, and Frank Ward back to his best form in 8th.
New Year's Day, and Frank Ward started the year off with 3rd place in the Cranleigh 10km in 30:39. Winner was Hugh Brasher of Hounslow in 30:31 with Omega's C.Harry 2nd in 30:33.

Over a 5 mile course at Banstead on March 1st it was a one-two for Belgrave with Frank Ward coming home in 25:21 and Marcello Bizio, 26:46. Another fine run came from Frank with his 30:33 for 3rd place in the Herne Hill '10' on March 15th.
Frank Ward won the club "five and three quarters" which in turn earned him the right to contest this, the strongest of all stages. He proved my faith in him with a superb 25:11.

We had sadly missed our key men all season and again Gary Staines, John Gladwin, Stuart Paton, Ollie Foote and Frank Ward were all still absent, added to which Ikem Billy was again injured while Steve Halliday was enjoying a 5 day prize holiday in Paris with Brandon Reid also on vacation.

Lenny Paul continued his programme of racing to peak fitness with a 10.8 clocking and Frank Ward took the 5000m in 15:01.0. Unfortunately our Treasurer then found himself suffering from an ankle injury.

… year's twelve stage team appeared, and with Marco Mazzotta dropping out with a bad back, Andy Paton clearly unfit, and Frank Ward arriving late, it was only the ever-reliable Jim Estall of those four who performed as expected.…

When shortly before the race Frank Ward was seen donning a pair of shoes bearing more than a trace of damp mud, it didn't really need a Sherlock Holmes to deduce that he had been hard at work on the hills of Streatham Common during the week.

It was newcomer James Ryle who again produced the best run of the day finishing in 11th position, just ahead of Frank Ward. Nice to see Frank gradually returning to fitness in time for the twelve stage.
Marcello Bizio led at the top of Lauriston Road with Frank Ward and Marco Mazzotta, both far more unfit than last year, hanging on at least for the first lap of the common.
Above: Frank Ward has spent the winter gradually regaining fitness and will be wanting to get well under 15 minutes again for 5,000m this summer.

…ll produced his usual reliable run in spite of high mileage marathon training: "Can't I run two legs ?" Then a half fit Frank Ward got round on memory to hand over to Steve Halliday, down from Halifax for the race, as cheery as ever and having a blinding run with 4th fastest long stage of the day to…

Conditions were bright and the going firm as the field set out, Captain 'Gerry' Adams at the head of the field and Frank Ward at the back, still divesting himself of his training kit while 150 metres into the race.
The longer events also saw Treasurer Frank Ward and our Italian steeplechasing duo back in action but we were somewhat depleted in other areas in spite of this being virtually a 'home' match.
With Alex Luce, Mike Lake, Mike Webb, Mark Anderson and Frank Ward all close behind, Belgrave would have made up for the loss at Croydon even without their stars.

Meanwhile, back at home our road race championship was taking place, and with one of the most unexpected comebacks since Lazarus, Frank Ward turned up to waltz off with a title that he surely must now have won more times than anyone else.
Bill pulled over and waited ... and sure enough it was exactly the man he thought it was: Frank Ward, a champion in our races several times and at one time our Hon.
